https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-08-03.text: PBS Shows Live TV PBS Shows Live TV On Air Now Playing KSKA 91.1 FM Latest News Federal agents detain a fifth Juneau man for immigration purposes KTOO | By Yvonne Krumrey, KTOO Published August 3, 2026 at 8:53 AM AKDT Twitter LinkedIn Email Bluesky Lisa Phu / KTOO Lemon Creek Correctional Center in Juneau. Another man was taken into custody in Juneau for immigration enforcement purposes and held in Lemon Creek Correctional Center last week. Alaska Department of Corrections spokesperson Betsy Holley said a man named Jose Manuel Rivera-Rivera was held at the Juneau prison on a federal custody hold from Wednesday through Friday. He was transferred to Anchorage Correctional Complex on Friday, she said. Juneau Police Chief Derek Bos told KTOO in an email that U.S. Customs and Border Protection conducted an operation Wednesday near Thunder Mountain Middle School, but said the Juneau Police Department was not involved. After the operation, however, Bos said CBP requested police assistance with a person in its custody. “A JPD officer responded and transported the individual away from the area for Border Patrol and was able to successfully de-escalate the incident," Bos wrote. Bos directed further questions to Customs and Border Protection. CPB Regional Press Officer Jason Givens said over email the arrest was part of an active investigation and that “no further information is available at this time.” It is unclear what federal charges Rivera-Rivera is being held under. According to VINE , an online database of incarcerated people, a 52-year-old man named Jose Rivera is being held at Anchorage Correctional Complex. Rivera-Rivera is the sixth person held at Lemon Creek under a federal custody hold for immigration purposes since October. Three men — Ernesto Alanzo Haro, Alfredo Gomez-Guzman, and Carlos Jara Medina — were detained and removed from Juneau in 2025. According to the Alaska Department of Corrections, Peter Verkin, a Slovakian man who had been living in Sitka, and another Juneau man , Darwin Mendez-Cando, were detained in February. One of the six men, Gomez-Guzman is still being held at Lemon Creek Correctional Center. He was originally detained and released to federal custody in November. It’s unclear what led to his return to Juneau. The other four arrests before Rivera-Rivera’s have all been transferred to federal custody outside of Alaska. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP Sydney Boy, 11, shot in the face and neck in Sydney dies from his injuries The 11-year-old died at Westmead children’s hospital three days after incident at a unit in Norwest Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Martin Farrer Thu 24 Sep 2026 08.15 EDT First published on Thu 24 Sep 2026 08.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A young boy who was allegedly shot at a home in Sydney’s north-west earlier this week has died. Police said that the boy, who had been in a critical condition since being found with a gunshot wound at a unit in Norwest on Monday, died in hospital at about 8pm on Thursday. Police had been called to the unit in Fairway Drive at about 5pm on Monday after reports of a shooting . Officers found the 11-year-old boy had sustained a gunshot wound to his face and neck. He was treated at the scene by NSW Ambulance paramedics before being taken to at Westmead Children’s hospital in a critical condition. Five other people who were in the home at the time of the incident were not injured. Three men, all aged 18, were arrested. Two were taken to The Hills police station and later released pending further inquiries. One of the men, Isaac Bechara, was charged with concealing a serious indictable offence, while two of the other men were arrested and released pending further inquiries. He appeared at Blacktown local court on Tuesday morning , where he made no application for bail, which was refused. Det Supt Naomi Moore told reporters on Tuesday afternoon that police were “aware” of the unit where the shooting had occurred and had “engaged with the occupants previously”. “This shooting at this stage does not appear to be linked directly to current conflicts however a number of individuals who were inside the unit at the time are well known to NSW police,” she said. “Their association with organised crime is being considered by investigators.” Police said the investigation was continuing. National Security Trump Announces ‘Major Progress’ in Establishing US Army Base in Poland Poland’s president thanked Trump for his commitment to the U.S.–Poland partnership. Approximately 10,000 U.S. troops are stationed in Poland. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print President Donald Trump and Polish President Karol Nawrocki head to the Oval Office on Sept. 3, 2025. Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images Timothy Frudd 9/17/2026 | Updated: 9/17/2026 0:00 X 1 Significant progress is being made toward the establishment of a U.S. Army base in Poland, according to President Donald Trump. Trump said the establishment of a U.S. Army base in the NATO member state would be a “historic step” for the alliance between the United States and Poland. The U.S. Army Garrison Poland currently has a presence in Poland but does not have a permanent base in the country. “GREAT NEWS! Thanks to the bold leadership of my friend, Karol Nawrocki, President of Poland, major progress is being made toward establishing a U.S. Army base in Poland,” he wrote in a Truth Social statement on Sept. 17. “If this happens, the location will be announced very soon.” Polish Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski said last month that Poland was holding discussions with Pentagon officials about establishing several U.S. military bases in the country. In response to Trump’s announcement on Thursday, Nawrocki thanked him for his strong commitment to the U.S.-Poland partnership. “We are ready to continue our efforts to strengthen our defense cooperation: seriously, responsibly, and always together,” he wrote in a statement on X. “I can assure you that the Polish government will do its utmost to provide the best possible location for the US Army base.” Related Stories EU Parliament Chief Backs ‘Associate Membership’ for Australia, New Zealand Poland Signs $4 Billion US Military Financing Agreement Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz also released a statement Thursday, describing Trump’s comments as a “very important declaration” and a confirmation of the strategic cooperation between the two countries. Following an Aug. 27 meeting of the North Atlantic Council at NATO’s headquarters in Brussels, Zalewski confirmed that he had met with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby regarding potential base plans. “The American presence in Poland can encompass various defense capabilities,” Zalewski told Polish Radio at the time. “We believe it doesn’t have to be concentrated in one place. Of course, there are several locations we want to discuss with the U.S. side where such a presence would be truly massive. However, we are still talking about several bases and several locations.” There are currently about 10,000 U.S. troops stationed in Poland. The U.S. military leads NATO’s enhanced Forward Presence Battle Group in the country and deploys a rotational armored brigade combat team as part of Operation Atlantic Resolve. Poland’s government formally requested that the U.S. military establish permanent bases in June after Trump pledged to send 5,000 additional U.S. troops to the country. Following the meeting in August, Zalewski suggested that the establishment of U.S. bases in Poland would be beneficial to the United States beyond the immediate reaction to the war between Russia and Ukraine. “A permanent U.S. presence would reflect America’s long-term strategic interest in the country, not merely respond to the recent activities of Russia,” he said. The Epoch Times reached out to the Pentagon, the U.S. Army, the White House, and the Polish Embassy and did not receive a response before publication time. Rep. Joe Wilson (R-S.C.), chairman of the U.S. Helsinki Commission, also known as the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe, expressed gratitude to Poland on Thursday for what he described as “amazing progress” toward the establishment of a U.S. Army base in the country. “Poland is a model ally and knows well that freedom is not free,” Wilson stated. “Peace through Strength requires strong deterrence. For our freedom and yours!” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) also applauded the development, suggesting that the best deterrence to Russian aggression was having a “forward presence” in Eastern Europe. The United States and Poland signed a $4 billion loan guarantee agreement on Sept. 9 that will allow Poland to purchase additional military equipment manufactured by the United States. NATO has estimated that Poland will have spent 4.68 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP) on defense in 2026, which puts the country among the highest spenders by GDP in the alliance.
